notes: All 100 EvoEval_difficult tasks, 3 runs per side, with both sides running at the same time in Daytona sandboxes built from the same Dockerfile (python:3.10.22-slim, numpy 2.2.6; 2 CPUs, 4 GB RAM). Both sides used the same pinned agent (mini-swe-agent 2.4.6), the same install command and the same command line (-c mini, --cost-limit 0, model timeout 3600 s, no max_tokens). Both requested the model as openai/deepseek-v4.1-flash through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Every response on both sides was served by the snapshot deepseek-v4-1-flash-261017. The instruction text is identical, and the agent timeout is 1800 s. While the agent runs, it can reach only the model API host: Harbor [agent] network_mode = no-network plus --allow-agent-host, and the same Daytona domain allowlist in the original-side runner. The agent environment on both sides sets UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER=2026-10-17T00:00:00Z, which resolves litellm 1.105.1, and LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True, so litellm does not fetch its cost map from GitHub. The original side is a fork of EvoEval with a runner that reproduces Harbor's agent setup. It scores the saved /workspace/solution.py with evoeval.evaluate plus one bugfix applied on both sides (float values must have the same number of elements). Unpatched upstream evoeval 0.1.0 gives the same original-side scores. Cross-scoring each side's 300 solutions with the other side's evaluator gave 0 disagreements. There were no infrastructure errors and no agent timeouts. Token usage over the two sanity checks and the three runs, both sides: about 16.4M prompt and 3.0M completion tokens.
